items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: started out as the dance music arranger for Carol Haney... I was with Carol. I did several of those shows... she was called and I was called with her to do shows like Bravo Giovanni, like Flower Drum Song

ctx.x: This is the second part of our interview, oral history with Mr. Luther Henderson, April 29th, 1993. Mr. Henderson, I want to talk about, yesterday we talked about your earlier musical beginnings, moving to New York, your work with Duke Ellington and I want to continue talking about your foray into Broadway. Tell me how you got into that.

How it happened? Well, I'll start back with my, how my interest was gotten into it very much so was by having seen the first company, the first performance, not the first performance but during the first company of Porgy and Bess which was 1935, in that area. And I was so impressed with how the jazz music that I'd been hearing in the streets and around and in records and so forth, how particularly it was adapted and went in to the theater and the scenery and the progress of the story and so forth.
